vehicles.headline: Confusable with vehicle 163
vehicles.why: Side by side with vehicle 163 at the same camera, and both go on to the same next one. Every space-time signal fires identically for the two of them.
vehicles.expect: Flag BOTH. Expect the ambiguity guard to fire: when two targets score within 0.10 of each other the system refuses to pick and sends it to review instead.

vehicles.headline: Crosses cameras with a real gap
vehicles.why: Left c009 and reappeared 16.58s later at another camera, with nothing observing it in between. That gap is the whole problem the system exists to solve.
vehicles.expect: Expect a candidate verdict on the second camera: the transit window supports it, but colour alone cannot name one car.

vehicles.headline: One hop supported, another refused
vehicles.why: 2 of its hops land inside the window real vehicles were observed to take, and 1 arrived faster than is physically possible. One car, evidence pointing both ways.
vehicles.expect: Expect the impossible hop to be rejected outright and the plausible ones to reach candidate. Watch the cascade panel disagree with itself across sightings -- that is the point.

vehicles.headline: Never once out of sight
vehicles.why: Its camera views overlap by up to 19.5s -- it is in two places' footage at once, so there is no unobserved gap to reason across.
vehicles.expect: Expect undecided, repeatedly. With no gap to cross, the transit signal never fires and colour alone scores below the threshold. A car the system honestly has nothing to say about.

vehicles.headline: The longest story in the scenario
vehicles.why: Visible for 101.7s across 4 cameras, the most footage any vehicle here gets.
vehicles.expect: Expect the appearance gallery to grow across many sightings, and the score to stay put anyway -- more looks at the same silver sedan is not more distinctive.

vehicles.headline: The least the system gets to work with
vehicles.why: Visible for only 3.2s across 3 cameras. Barely enough pixels to build a profile from.
vehicles.expect: Expect a candidate anyway. A few seconds of footage and one plausible hop is enough for the system to narrow -- which is exactly why narrowing is not the same as identifying.
